title: UI test framework
summary: Exercises scripted input, UI trees and committed frames, clock and settle behavior, failure evidence, and end-to-end scenarios with planted faults in GUI sessions.

cases.title: A clean scenario run in the inner executor returns Pass
A scenario with a planted pixel fault returns pixel-mismatch with its check and first pixel
A double-forked orphan is reparented to and reaped by its session supervisor, or by the runner when the supervisor died first
type_text("hello world") puts exactly that text in the focused text field
Characters that need Shift arrive correctly
Characters outside the keymap arrive through a text event
Newline and Tab arrive as the Enter and Tab keys
chord(Ctrl, A) arrives as A with the Ctrl modifier
Holding a key for 600 ms of UI time gives exactly 3 repeats
click(node) lands on a visible point of the node, and the delivery names that node's window
Clicking a node partly covered by another window lands on its exposed part, confirmed by hit test
Clicking a node clipped by a scrolled container uses its visible part
double_click delivers click counts 1 and 2
A ten-step drag reaches its captured node in order through layout changes and a window move, ending with nothing held
scroll(node, dy) delivers the wheel amount to the window under the node
Typing into a node focuses it first, and a node that cannot take focus fails by name
delivered(serial) returns only after the target window processed that serial
An event sent to a hung app is reported unprocessed at the 2 s settle bound, naming the serial and window
Every serial of a script ends with a terminal disposition
A non-root session cannot inject, after a root session has
Ending a session releases every held key and button
Input arrives in order while the app animates
Input addressed to two windows of one app arrives at each
A scripted Super double tap opens the launcher through bwm's real hotkey path
Events from a device outside the session's selection, modifier keys included, change nothing in the session
The test app's tree lists every widget with its expected role and key
Names and values match the widgets' states set by the script
The focused flag moves with Tab
The focused widget draws the theme's focus ring at its bounds
A disabled button is flagged not enabled
Checked, selected and pressed flags follow interaction
A text field's value equals the typed text
A terminal node's rows, cell attributes and cursor equal what its grid holds
A tree and its pixels always come from the same commit
bwm's tree lists each window's title, bounds, z order, focus and minimized state
Nodes scrolled out or covered are flagged not visible, with their clip
Scrolling a list changes which items are flagged visible
An unrelated non-root process cannot map another app's tree
With no reader attached the tree is never serialized, and with one it is serialized once per commit
A label whose tree text is PASS is checked against the certified renderer's PASS at its bounds
A window capture equals the committed buffer of that commit
Capturing commit N while the app draws N+1 returns N whole
A resize during a capture gives the whole old commit, pixels and tree, never ENOENT or a mixture
A screen capture shows the window at its position, with its observation record
A screen capture lists the commit of each window it contains
Captures taken with the cursor hidden contain no cursor pixels
The test app's canonical scene hashes to the pinned value on this target
Comparing two 1280x800 frames takes at most 50 ms
An app reading the UI clock sees it stand still between steps
step(16) advances the app's clock by exactly 16 ms and the epoch by one
Each step is acknowledged by every required participant in its commit metadata
An app's one-second timer fires on step(1000), not on real time
Wall-clock time shown by apps and bwm is the fixed instant plus elapsed UI time
bwm's taskbar clock and repeat timer read the UI clock
Two apps in one session step together
A stopped participant makes step fail naming it, unless the case excluded it
Stepping never deadlocks against buffer back-pressure
An app that animates forever still lets every step complete
An app's real-clock read counter stays 0 in a session and rises when the test app reads the real clock on purpose
Injected events carry UI time, and bwm's double-click threshold uses it
settle returns once nothing changes
settle waits until the target window commits with the serial processed, not until it reads the event
An app that drains events and never commits makes settle fail, naming the window and the serial
An event that changes nothing settles through commit_no_change
settle waits until a completed composite lists every visible window at its newest pixel generation
Settling after a commit_no_change completes through the composite that already holds the window's pixels
An idle step settles through bwm's none-needed acknowledgment, with the composite counter unchanged
A hotkey settles with no client involved, through its WM-handled disposition
settle waits for a named tree predicate on an asynchronous result
A settle that cannot complete fails, naming the window, serial or predicate it waited for
settle returns while an app has a future animation deadline
A minimized window acknowledges and processes without being waited on for pixels until it is restored
Repeated settle calls with nothing changing cause no extra frames
A desktop session with one app reaches its first composited commit within 300 ms
A kiosk session with one app reaches its first composited commit within 300 ms
Apps in a session receive its fonts, clock, seed, mode, time zone, locale and config root
bwm, Breengel's font configuration and every app read and write under the session's config root
A session that changes every setting leaves the global configuration files unchanged
A case killed while changing settings is followed by a case that sees the defaults
Two settings scenarios give the same results in either order
After a case its virtual devices are gone and no key or button is held
After a case, no session process remains and the runner owns the display
A hung app is killed and reaped at teardown
A screen capture during a case contains no panel pixels
When a session's compositor dies, the display goes to the session supervisor, then to the runner at case end
A scenario that runs out of time fails, and its evidence is saved inside the reserve
An app crashing during a scenario fails it, naming the app and the signal
An app launched as uid 1000 runs in the session while the harness keeps root observation
Twenty sessions in a row leave windows, processes and memory at the baseline
wait_window(title) returns after that window's first composited commit
wait_window for a window that never appears fails, naming the title
launch passes argv and the environment exactly
A mismatch saves the got image, diff image, tree, input log and screen
A passing case saves nothing unless saving is turned on
With saving turned on, a passing case saves its frames
The saved input log lists every serial with its disposition
The saved screen is the readback at the failing step, with its record
When the case process is killed, the runner sends end collect, waits for done before sweeping, and the evidence is on disk
An app that dies right after a commit still has that commit and tree saved, from its remnant
A widget drawn in the wrong color fails as pixel-mismatch with both colors
An app that updates its tree but not its pixels fails as pixel-mismatch
An app that drops one key fails as tree-mismatch on the text field's value
A hung app fails as app-hung when the 2 s step bound passes, instead of hanging the suite
Filling the test app's form (text field, checkbox, slider, submit) gives the expected tree and frame
Opening a menu and choosing an item gives the expected tree and frame
Scrolling and selecting in a list gives the expected tree and frame
A scripted focus scenario on bwm gives the expected trees and screens
A scripted stacking scenario on bwm gives the expected trees and screens
